note: One orbit-classification rule, written three times: classifyOrbit() in src/orbit.ts, derive_orbit() in pipeline/build_release.py, and regime_from_elements() in pipeline/catalog_audit.py. The audit copy is deliberately independent -- an audit that imports what it audits audits nothing -- so the copies cannot be collapsed, and this fixture is what keeps them one rule instead. Both tests/orbit-classifier-parity.test.ts and tests/test_orbit_classifier_parity.py read THIS file, so a change to the rule in any one language fails in the other two. A disagreement between the artifact's published `orbit` field and the client's own classifier would be a silent split-brain: nothing on the page shows it.
inputs: meanMotion (rev/day), eccentricity, inclinationDeg -- each side derives perigee, apogee and period itself

19.999 deg is still GEO

1499.5 min is inside the window
